meta.title: Athletics Command Center — Sponsorship & event logistics software | Flux Athletics
meta.description: The Athletics Command Center gives athletic departments one system for sponsorship inventory and fulfillment, event staffing, run-of-show and game day logistics.

hero.title: The operating system for your season.
hero.lead: Sponsorship obligations, event staffing and game day logistics in one place — so an athletic department running forty events a month can see all of them at once.

stats.v: Shared source of truth for sponsorship, staffing and logistics — instead of three systems that disagree.
Contracted obligation tracked to a date, an event and a person responsible for delivering it.
Long records that survive staff turnover, so next year’s team starts from what worked.

problem.heading: The work is not hard. Keeping track of it is.
problem.lead: A single home football Saturday can carry a hundred contracted obligations, a hundred and fifty staff shifts and a dozen vendors on load-in windows that overlap. None of it is complicated on its own. All of it at once, across every sport, in spreadsheets and texts, is how things get missed.

items.title: Obligations slip quietly
items.body: A missed PA read or video board spot rarely gets noticed until a partner asks for a recap at renewal time.

items.title: Staffing runs on memory
items.body: Who works which gate, who confirmed, who no-showed last time — usually known by one person, stored nowhere.

items.title: Nothing carries forward
items.body: When a coordinator leaves, the run-of-show and the vendor relationships tend to leave with them.

modules.heading: What’s inside.
modules.lead: Start with the piece that hurts most. Add the rest when you are ready — everything shares the same calendar, the same venues and the same people.

items.title: Sponsorship inventory
items.body: Every asset you sell — signage, PA reads, video board, digital, hospitality — catalogued once, with its own availability, rate and owner.

items.title: Obligation tracking
items.body: Contracts become a checklist of deliverables mapped to specific dates and events, so a missed read is caught the same week, not at renewal.

items.title: Proof of performance
items.body: Capture the evidence as it happens — timestamps, photos, as-run logs — and generate the recap a partner will actually renew against.

items.title: Event staffing
items.body: Build shift templates per sport and venue, publish openings, assign crews, and track who confirmed, who checked in and who is short.

items.title: Run of show
items.body: One shared timeline per event: load-in, rehearsal, promos, activations, media timeouts. Everyone works from the same document, live.

items.title: Vendors & venues
items.body: Keep vendor contacts, load-in windows, access requirements and venue-specific rules attached to the event instead of buried in email.

items.title: Multi-sport scheduling
items.body: See the whole athletic calendar at once — overlapping events, shared staff, shared spaces — and catch conflicts before they are a Saturday problem.

items.title: Reporting
items.body: Season-level views of fulfillment rate, staffing coverage and cost, ready to hand to a director, a partner or a board.

items.title: Audit
items.body: We inventory what you sell and what you staff, and identify where obligations are currently being tracked — or not.

items.title: Configure
items.body: Your sports, venues, shift templates and partner contracts are loaded in, so the system reflects how your department actually operates.

items.title: Run a live event
items.body: We are on site or on call for your first events, training the staff who will own it day to day.

items.q: Who is the Command Center built for?
items.a: Athletic departments, conferences and venue operators who run a lot of events with a small full-time staff — the operations, marketing and external relations side rather than compliance or academics.

items.q: Do we have to move everything at once?
items.a: No. Most groups start with one problem — usually sponsorship fulfillment or event staffing — get a season under their belt, then expand. The system is designed to be useful on day one with a single module in use.

items.q: Can it work alongside our ticketing and CRM systems?
items.a: Yes. The Command Center is built to sit on the operations layer, not replace your ticketing or donor systems. We will map the handoffs during implementation.
It depends on how many sports and venues you run and how much of your inventory is already documented. We scope that in the audit before anyone signs anything.

items.q: What happens when our staff turns over?
items.a: That is a large part of the point. Templates, run-of-show documents and fulfillment records stay with the department rather than leaving with the person who built them.

cta.title: See it against your own season.
cta.body: Send us a real weekend from your calendar and we will walk you through how the Command Center would have handled it.
cta.label: Request a walkthrough

meta.title: Broadcaster's Toolkit — Live sports graphics & plugins | Flux Athletics
meta.description: The Broadcaster's Toolkit from Flux Athletics: score bugs, lower thirds, sponsor billboards, stat pages and plugins that make a small live sports crew look broadcast-grade.

hero.title: Make a small crew look like a network.
hero.lead: Plugins and graphics packages for live sports production. Built for the people running a show with two cameras, one operator and no margin for error.

preview.caption: Representative layout. Every package is rebuilt in your colours, type and naming.

kit.heading:
Everything a
sports show
needs on screen.
kit.lead: Not a folder of loose templates. A designed package where the score bug, the lower third and the sponsor read all share the same rules — and an operator can drive the whole thing alone.

items.title: Scoreboard & clock bugs
items.body: Score bugs that read from your clock and scoring source, styled to your brand, with the states a real game needs — timeouts, period breaks, overtime, final.

items.title: Lower thirds
items.body: Name keys, stat cards, matchup comparisons and interview keys built as a set, so every insert in your show looks like it belongs to the same package.

items.title: Sponsor billboards
items.body: Full-frame and corner-bug sponsor elements with rotation logic, plus an as-run log you can hand back to the partner as proof.

items.title: Stat pages
items.body: Leaders, box scores, team comparisons and season lines — populated from your data source rather than retyped between whistles.

items.title: Transitions & stings
items.body: Wipes, bumpers and open animations cut to your package so a stream returning from break feels produced instead of abrupt.

items.title: Ticker & social
items.body: Scrolling scores, promotional messaging and moderated social pulls for the bottom of the frame.

compat.heading: Built for the tools you already run.
compat.lead: We deliver into the switcher and CG workflow your crew knows, rather than asking you to rebuild the truck around a new piece of software. Tell us what you run and we will confirm the delivery format before you commit.
compat.note: CONFIRM this list matches what Flux Athletics actually supports today.

items.title: Software switchers
items.body: Packages delivered for common software production stacks, driven by title inputs your operator already understands.

items.title: Browser-based overlays
items.body: HTML overlay sources that key over program in any tool that accepts a browser input — and update live from your data.

items.title: Scoring & stat feeds
items.body: Wired to your clock, scoring console or stat provider so the numbers on screen are not being typed by hand.

items.title: Operator control
items.body: A simple control surface for the person running graphics, built so a student operator can be trained in an afternoon.

items.title: Brand it
items.body: We take your marks, colours and type and build the package around them — including the sponsor treatments your partners have already bought.

items.title: Wire it
items.body: Graphics are connected to your clock, scoring and stat sources, and installed into your production stack ahead of a live date.

items.title: Train it
items.body: We run a rehearsal with the crew who will operate it, then stay reachable for your first broadcasts of the season.

cta.title: Tell us what your show looks like.
cta.body: Send us your stack, your sports and a link to a recent broadcast. We will come back with what the Toolkit would change.
cta.label: Get the Toolkit

why.heading: We do not hand you a deck and leave

When we tell you inventory should be repackaged or a staffing model should change, we can show you the system that makes it hold up over a full season - and we are there when it goes live.

items.title: Partner activation

items.title: Brand & marketing

engagements.heading:
Three ways
to work
together.

items.title: The audit
items.body: A fixed-scope review of your sponsorship inventory, event operation or broadcast workflow, ending in a written set of findings and a prioritised list of what to fix first.

items.title: The build
items.body: We design the thing and stand it up with you — a new partnership package, an event plan, a staffing model, a production standard — through to its first live use.

items.title: The season

items.title: Listen

items.title: Recommend

items.title: Implement
items.body: We stay through execution, whether that means standing up the Command Center, rebuilding a package, or working the event with you.

hero.title: We build for the people off the field
hero.lead: Flux Athletics creates software, tools and strategy for the side of sports the crowd never sees - the operations, partnerships and production work that makes game day smooth.

intro.heading:
One company,
multiple fronts.
paragraphs: We stared from a simple observation: most athletic departments are severely understaffed and typically rely on volunteers, students and parents to help make game day happen.

So we continue to work tirelessly to create solutions, including our Athletics Command Center for sponsorship and gameday logistics, broadcast toolkits for those that can't be in the stadium or arena, and consulting for decisions that software can't make for you.

beliefs.heading:
Four things
we keep
coming back to

items.title: Operations
items.body: The game is the visible part. For most athletic departments, winning on the field is only part of the equation for what makes a successful season.

items.title: Tools should fit the crew you have
items.body: Nobody has an adequately sized staff. Everything we build assumes fewer people, not more.

items.title: Prove it or do not sell it
items.body: A sponsorship is worth what you can demonstrate you deliver. We build for evidence because renewals are won with it.

items.title: Simple beats complete
items.body: A system people actually use every day is work more than a complicated one they abandon within a few months.
